input.public_request: You are defining a small greenfield feature for a text-only greeter. Produce an implementation-ready requirement for: "Add an optional farewell line after greeting output." Your answer must make the exact output shape judgeable, including where the farewell appears relative to the greeting, what makes it appear or not appear, the exact farewell text/format, and at least one example where the farewell is present and one otherwise similar example where it is absent.

material_decisions.answer: The farewell, when enabled, is part of the same text output as the greeting and appears as a second line immediately after the greeting line. The greeting remains the first line. No separate message, channel, or inline same-line variant is allowed.
material_decisions.why_material: This removes ambiguity about the output boundary and makes implementations converge on one observable shape.

material_decisions.answer: The farewell is controlled by a single boolean input flag named `includeFarewell`. When `includeFarewell` is `true`, the farewell line is included; when `false`, it is omitted. The default is `false` if the flag is not provided.
material_decisions.why_material: This defines who decides the conditional behavior and prevents incompatible assumptions about context, configuration, or heuristics.

material_decisions.answer: The farewell line is exactly `Goodbye.` including capitalization and the period, with no added names, emojis, or alternate punctuation.
material_decisions.why_material: A fixed literal contract is necessary so reviewers can distinguish intended output from arbitrary variants.

material_decisions.answer: Canonical examples: with input name `Sam` and `includeFarewell=true`, output is exactly `Hello, Sam!\nGoodbye.`. With the same name and `includeFarewell=false`, output is exactly `Hello, Sam!`. No extra trailing line is emitted when the flag is false.
material_decisions.why_material: Matched positive and negative examples prove both the changed and unchanged behaviors and make regression checks straightforward.

owner_rules: Accept only answers that make the output reproducible verbatim from the stated rules and examples.
Reject answers that use words like optional, maybe, or if needed without an explicit activation mechanism.
Reject answers that describe the farewell conceptually but do not freeze its exact text and punctuation.
Reject answers that provide only the enabled case or only the disabled case.

open_material_decisions: What exact farewell line should be added, and should it always appear as a new line after the greeting when enabled?

question.prompt: This changes the exact observable output and acceptance tests. Choose the farewell line behavior when the optional farewell is enabled.

options.label: New line: Goodbye!
options.description: Append a second line exactly `Goodbye!` after the greeting; simplest and most judgeable.

options.label: Same line: Goodbye!
options.description: Append ` Goodbye!` on the same line as the greeting; shorter output but different formatting contract.

options.label: Custom text/placement
options.description: Provide your own exact farewell text and whether it appears on a new line or the same line.

When enabled, append a second line immediately after the greeting line. The farewell line is exactly `Goodbye.`. The greeting remains the first line.

Activation: controlled only by `includeFarewell`; default `false` when omitted.

Examples:
- `name=Sam, includeFarewell=true` -> `Hello, Sam!\nGoodbye.`
- `name=Sam, includeFarewell=false` -> `Hello, Sam!`
